scope: Seven canonical Transformation halls; final-text illustrations only.

plates.title: WHAT SURVIVES ITS MOVEMENT?
plates.focus: Collection and animation are different capabilities. Successive operations preserve different properties; demonstrations remain available while pickups disappear.
plates.summary: A still cube can be collected. Other cubes rise, turn and swell; smaller markers isolate each addition. Their movement leaves different things to recognise.
panels: Even without an animation, it can be collected.

Student watches an utterly still cream cube at body height, then approaches on level floor. Nearby a small paired moment shows the cube disappears when the visitor walks into it, not when grabbed. No hand holding it.
Its position changes while its size and facing stay the same.

One cube bobs vertically. A thin Y-up motion overlay shows lower and upper poses with IDENTICAL size and facing; solid cube one, other poses dashed. Small adjacent marker isolates vertical translation.
The rise and the turn continue together.
Next cream cube rises and turns around upright Y. A marked corner and understated circular/vertical motion arrows show two operations. No tumbling pitch or rolling around a horizontal axis.
All three dimensions change together, so it keeps its cube shape.
The fourth example rises, turns and pulses uniformly. An inset contains small and large CUBES of equal proportions, not a stretched box. A single cube per real station.
The three moving examples remain.
Look back at original four stations: first collected station empty, three animated demonstration cubes still present. Student looks without collecting these demonstration specimens.
Each operation has left something to recognise.

On raised path reached by wedges, four finished animated pickups. Student walks into one, which swells then disappears; other three continue. Background demonstrations remain running below. No claim whole hall pauses.
plates.footer: The next hall asks which of these changes can give us somewhere to stand.

plates.title: THE FAR BANK IS ALREADY THERE
plates.focus: An operation supplies passage only through agreements with support, landing and timing. Moving the background can undo a working crossing.
plates.summary: Travel, growth and a quarter-turn offer three temporary surfaces across fire basins. Moving the far bank changes whether the same plank can reach it.
plates.reference_note: Image 2 shows the actual orange plank, fire basin, railed far bank and MOVE THE BANK instrument. Reinterpret this architecture in the comic style; keep the exposed gap beyond the same plank.
panels: What would have to change for it to become somewhere you can go?
Student stands safely at near bank of a floor-level gap. Fire glows BELOW in basin. Far landing visible, not yet reachable. No glass floor over this hazard, no person falling or being injured.
Relative to the room, you are moving. Relative to the cube, you may be standing still.
Student stands level on a cube carrier moving horizontally over fire. Feet stay on top, body upright. Near bank recedes, far bank approaches. Cube keeps size and facing.
What made a floor a moment ago is withdrawing below it.

Green cube grows about a fixed centre BELOW floor so its top reaches both banks at full size, then shrinks. Paired schematic full/small poses show top aligned with floor only when large; growth also extends down, not only up.
The centre stays in place while the end sweeps a curve around it.

Thin orange plank turns horizontally around upright Y; a quarter-turn aligns its long ends with banks. Top stays floor-level, centre fixed. Show before across route versus aligned route with small overhead inset. No pitch, vertical paddle or tilted slope here.
You have moved the place it needs to reach.

Matched overhead diagrams: same orange plank length, angle and centre, and same near bank. Far bank sits edge-to-edge in one view and farther away on rails in the other, leaving visible gap. Student moves MOVE THE BANK slider. Plank unchanged.
A place to stand can also be a moment you have to meet.
Student waits beside aligned plank for its pause, companion looks toward moving timer-independent crossings. They remain on safe bank. Show return aisle around gap, not an unavoidable lethal route.
plates.footer: The simulation supplies an opening and a duration.

plates.title: SEVEN JOURNEYS
plates.focus: Displacement can carry a body without turning it. Repeated routes and vanished pickups leave different records; a shared destination does not mean shared permissions.
plates.summary: Carriers move sideways, into depth, upward and along combined directions. At the exit, guided and free handles can reach the same endpoint through different permitted journeys.
panels: Direction of travel and direction of attention have separated.
Student faces down hall while a level cube carrier translates sideways X. Simple horizontal travel arrow and gaze into depth; cube orientation remains fixed. Fire basin below, safe islands at ends.
The carrier changes y; the room gives that change a consequence.
Level lift carries upright student to a higher fixed landing. Lower landing remains where it was, below. One vertical Y arrow; no entire room dropping or rotating.
Its surface stays level while its path slopes.

Carrier moves down and forward together on straight diagonal path toward low landing. Student remains upright on level top; ghost start/end carrier poses have same facing and size. No ramp that pitches the carrier.
The carrier can repeat the journey; the cube is gone.
Small pickup disappears as the carrier brings the rider into it. Next-moment inset carrier returns past the now EMPTY pickup place. Rider does not take object in hand.
We have combined directions without adding rotation.

High oblique view of a level carrier travelling diagonally X and Z across a basin. Its edges remain parallel to room axes in start/end dashed overlay; neither carrier nor rider must face direction of travel.
Your hand can propose a diagonal and leave a vertical line.

Two door mechanisms on matching plinth frames. Guided handle has vertical-then-horizontal rail and pale L-shaped accepted trail. Free handle has diagonal trail to the SAME relative endpoint in its own frame. Subtle dotted proposed hand diagonal beside guided handle, clearly separate from its actual recorded L route. Red and blue door panels, no unequal target distances.
plates.footer: A destination can be shared by journeys with very different permissions.

plates.title: ROOM FOR A TURN
plates.focus: Rotation, upright carriage and access require different rules. Wider bodies can slide differently; operation order matters; a returned outline need not return a marked face.
plates.summary: A level platform accompanies a turning blade. Angled cubes admit different routes, two turns exchange order, and sweep contours keep the space of a whole turn in view.
panels: Keeping you upright requires a rule alongside the turn.

Orange blade rotates about horizontal X like a paddle. Student stands on a separate LEVEL platform mounted to its SIDE, clear of blade sweep; platform follows arc up toward high landing while rider stays upright. Never put student upside down or on the blade during vertical pose.
Wider need not mean less room to move.

Fixed band of rotated cubes has ridges. Cyan narrow capsule trial caught on ridge; pink wider capsule trial slides sideways and continues. Same heights and forward instruction. These are simple capsule proxies, no living people trapped, no jump arrows; slides supplied by collisions.
The second receives the orientation left by the first.

Clear workbench diagram: one finned starting form in pale grey, blue sequence X then Y versus red sequence Y then X. Results retain SAME shape and size but fins point in different directions. Same local origin, separated for display only. Labels X then Y / Y then X, no translation offset claimed as difference.
What returned depends on what you were following.

Matched cube views at zero and quarter-turn about Y. Cube outline identical; pale L mark goes from one side face to another. Labels 0° / 90°. Mark rotates with cube, not painted onto same face in both views.
A turn needs room that a single pose leaves empty.

Amber cube paused inside cyan explanatory CYLINDER sweep contour around upright axis. Adjacent amber right-triangle face, upright edge on axle, inside cyan CONE sweep contour. Wireframe contours contain empty space and are not solid walls. Cube and triangle remain actual shapes.
The rule after release quietly takes the last word.

Small hinged plate with neighbour plates. Paired KEEP pose held after release and RETURN moving back toward stored angle. Student's hands released, sparse dashed corner traces differ. The object's hinge support fixed, no living sculpture or artist portrait.

plates.title: A DOOR, AT LAST
plates.focus: The room grows fourfold while the body remains fixed; relocation is a second operation. Preserved proportions do not preserve bodily access.
plates.summary: A tiny doorway becomes an exit when a furnished room enlarges. The same body is separately placed on the table, then descends a landscape of serving plates toward a fixed museum frame.
plates.reference_note: Image 2 is actual before/after gold door comparison. Tiny door 0.45 by 0.60m; enlarged door 1.8 by 2.4m. Museum's second gold frame stays ordinary size. Preserve this relative scale; comic student remains adult-sized.
panels: Calling it an exit describes somebody else's possibility.

Adult student beside a tiny gold doorway, only about knee height. Furnished miniature room with food tower, porcelain plates and sculptural female figure in crystal-studded suit with leaning panels. Door visible but too small for body. No crouching magically through.
What could be read at a glance now asks for a journey.

Student reaches for small DRINK ME bottle on highest serving plate before change. Small comparison inset then places SAME adult student standing on an ENLARGED top plate, the food and crystal figure now architectural. No student shrinking, bottle remains absent after taking.
The room and its contents are suddenly four times as large.

Paired schematic before/after furnished room: object sizes AND distances between furniture grow proportionally. Adult body SAME height both. Labels Room ×4 / Body unchanged. No smooth swelling animation: abrupt cut, no scaled walking speed or gravity claim.
The room has changed size, and you have been given a new place from which to meet it.

Student at top of giant food tower, feet on porcelain, looks down winding serving-plate descent. Emphasise separate placement on top and continuous potential route down; not scale automatically carrying them there.
There is a difference between preserving a shape and preserving what someone can do there.

Adult passes enlarged gold doorway now full-sized, then sees second gold frame beyond SAME size that stayed fixed. Tiny door before shown as small inset, same adult reference. Same door proportions, different access; no giant museum frame.
The code can name a clearance. It cannot decide whose body ought to be the measure.

Sparse separate wall with width-adjustable opening, dark offset disc and floor strip continuing through too-narrow gap. Student chooses side aisle; small wider-setting inset offers passage. Body and opening height fixed. No claim one size fits everyone.
plates.footer: Your approach will be enough to make the surroundings respond.

plates.title: THE INVITATION HAS DIMENSIONS
plates.focus: Proximity can change a boundary without removing its parts. A cut changes the count and leaves a cell-sized record; reversible responses and retained absence differ.
plates.summary: Slats turn toward an approaching visitor, a low lattice loses cells, and nearby blocks shrink. Two boundaries return after departure; one keeps the cut.
panels: A doorway has come to meet you.

Upright wall of thin vertical slats rotates those nearest approaching student. Local opening follows visitor position, no handle or automatic sliding solid wall; slats rotate about their vertical axes.
You have crossed the boundary before you have left its attention.
Student beyond slats but still close: neighbouring slats remain open. Separate small later view after student retreats shows slats closed again. Parts all retained, no destroyed planks.
Your eyes had crossed this space before your body could.
Low cube lattice only 1.3m tall, adult head sees over top, legs face solid cells. No full-height wall, cave ceiling or floor pit. Student leans to look beyond without crossing legs yet.
The next step becomes possible because something has been removed.

Walking through low lattice creates OPEN-TOPPED trench with stepped cell edges. No displaced cubes piled at side, no shrink or transparent ghost cells. Absent cells truly absent. Student legs enter cleared floor-level route.
All nine blocks are still there. Your distance has become their size.
Three-by-three array of exactly nine blocks, nearest ones shrink to make gap for student. Their horizontal centres stay fixed; bases stay on floor. Far blocks full size, no missing cells.
Two boundaries return; one keeps the cut.
Quiet comparison after visitor walks away: slat wall closed; low lattice retains open-topped trench; nine blocks returned to full size. Three small matched scenes, no clock-caused cell healing.
plates.footer: You will have to find your moment.

plates.title: YOUR AVAILABLE SPACE IS THE REMAINDER
plates.focus: Timed transformations can occupy a visitor's place without approach. A body-responsive composite door turns the same operations into welcome with chosen conditions.
plates.summary: Pushers, turning slabs and growers follow their own timing on level ground. An armoured door then translates, turns and shrinks on approach to make a usable opening.
panels: You meet a wall that arrives.

Red block with directional arrow travels across level floor toward route; student waits in clear SIDE AISLE, not standing atop or being crushed. Block keeps dimensions. No fire pit in this hall; ground level.
The space this slab sweeps through is larger than the space one pose shows.

Upright orange wall slab rotates around fixed vertical centre. Solid current pose broad face and dashed alternate edge-on pose, swept floor arc overlay. Visitor stands outside sweep. No horizontal walkable plank mistaken for this slab.
They grow anyway.
Student holds still near three cubes growing together at elapsed-time rhythm. No proximity arrows from student, no sensing halos. Safe open area to watch; floor level.
The gap has no such guarantee.

Matched small/large cube views from same camera. Both bottom edges stay ON FLOOR. Cube expands upward and sideways, uniformly; gap to neighbouring structure shrinks. Small cube green, large warmer colour. Body same size both.
The frame has stayed still. The passage has changed.

Armoured door with TWO leaves: three matched small views closed, turning, open. Each leaf moves sideways/up, rotates within doorway face about Z, shrinks into side recess. Frame stays same size and position; visible/collision opening coherent.
Its welcome has a reach, a width and a waiting time, each chosen in advance.

Student and companion pass through fully open fixed frame. Small later inset after everybody has left shows door returning closed, with caption only Later. No door closing onto people; no universal unconditional welcome.
plates.footer: There they made a small object conspicuous. Here they make room for you.
